llm.summary: This is a coherent PicSee MCP documentation skill, but users should understand it can create, edit, delete, and analyze PicSee links after OAuth authorization.

dimensions.detail: External calls to api.picsee.io and public-api-oauth.picsee.io are necessary for the service; optional QR/chart recipes send short links or analytics data to third-party renderers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Most installation paths use direct MCP HTTP configuration, while the optional stdio fallback uses unpinned npx mcp-remote, which introduces supply-chain risk if used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Authenticated use grants user:read and user:write for the PicSee account; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but edit/delete actions should be user-directed and confirmed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself ships no executable code and claims not to store tokens, but OAuth tokens are persisted by the user's MCP client and migration docs include narrowly scoped cleanup deletion commands for old v2 files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: URL shortening, link management, analytics, QR/chart recipes, and PicSee MCP registration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable connecting your agent to PicSee and granting OAuth user:read/user:write. Prefer the direct Streamable HTTP MCP setup; avoid the npx bridge unless needed, and pin or control the bridge dependency in managed environments. Confirm any edit or delete operation before allowing the agent to change account links, and do not shorten URLs or render charts that contain secrets, private identifiers, signed parameters, or sensitive analytics.
llm.findings:
[AS1] expected: The referenced .gemini and .codex paths are installation instructions for adding MCP config, not evidence that the skill reads agent configuration or credentials.
[AS2] expected: The mcp_config.json reference is a user-facing configuration path for registering the PicSee MCP endpoint, not hidden MCP discovery or abuse.
[TM1] expected: The rm commands are optional v2 migration cleanup steps limited to PicSee token and old CLI artifact paths; they are risky if copied blindly but not purpose-mismatched or deceptive.
[E1] expected: Transmission to api.picsee.io is central to the PicSee URL-shortening and analytics service and is clearly disclosed.
[T08] expected: The optional stdio bridge uses unpinned npx mcp-remote, which is a real supply-chain weakness, but it is disclosed as a compatibility fallback rather than hidden executable payload.
[other] expected: The QR and chart recipes disclose optional use of api.qrserver.com and quickchart.io; users should avoid those recipes for sensitive links or analytics.
